content.title: About
content.content: Nuts are edible seeds of various woody plants cultivated in warm regions worldwide. They have a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a crunchy texture. Nuts are eaten raw, roasted, or blanched and are used in baking, desserts, spreads, and plant‑based milks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nuts belong to the Rosaceae family and are related to peaches, plums, and cherries.
There are sweet and bitter varieties; bitter nuts contain toxic compounds and are not sold as regular snacks.
Nut trees have been cultivated for several thousand years.
Nuts are processed into flour, butter, marzipan, and plant milks.
Nut blossoms appear in early spring, before the leaves emerge.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Nuts are one of the best plant sources of vitamin E, an antioxidant that helps protect cells.

items.title: Provides healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Most of the fat in nuts is monounsaturated, which can support heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Provides protein and fiber
items.content: Nuts contribute plant protein and dietary fiber, which promote satiety.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Nuts contain more calcium than most other nuts, benefiting bone health.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Nuts can trigger allergic reactions, which may be severe in some individuals.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Nuts are calorie‑dense, so portion sizes should be moderate.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Whole nuts are not suitable for young children because they can cause choking.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Nuts contain oxalates; people prone to kidney stones may need to limit intake. Bitter nuts should never be eaten raw.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Nuts can be eaten as a snack, added to oatmeal, yogurt, salads, and baked goods, or ground into nut flour and butter. Soaking or blanching softens the skins and makes them easier to remove. Unsalted or lightly salted nuts are a good choice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store nuts in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer storage, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent oil rancidity. Discard nuts that smell bitter, sharp, or stale.
